plan.title: One Directive launch root per host session: a worker's session:ready rebinds it and locks the parent and siblings out of their worktrees

narratives.Description: When a checkout's Directive runtime is linked in from a different checkout through a directory junction, the hook takes its launch root from the runtime's real path, lands in the other checkout, and refuses every hooked call as a host-root mismatch whose recovery cannot help. Nothing warns before that first refusal. This story keeps the root check exactly as strict, names the linked-in case `foreign-runtime-link` with a recovery that clears it, and adds a direct runtime-ownership check to doctor and session start so the link is caught before work begins. The earlier theory in the issue title (a worker's session:ready moving a shared session root) did not survive the design arc; the bound contract is successor lean 6811136862 (accepted synthesis 6811234519).
narratives.Overview:
1. `packages/runtime/src/hook-dispatch.ts` `run()`: on a root mismatch, cut `process.argv[1]` with `resolveLaunchingCheckoutRootFromPath`. When that link-side root equals payloadRoot and the real-path launchRoot does not, deny with reason `foreign-runtime-link`, naming both roots. The link-side root selects wording only; it is never an admission input. Every other mismatch keeps today's deny.
2. `foreign-runtime-link` recovery (`install-health/constants.ts`): from a terminal outside the locked session, remove the link at `<payloadRoot>/node_modules` or `<payloadRoot>/node_modules/@deftai/directive-runtime` and install the runtime in `<payloadRoot>`. Stated outcome: this clears the foreign-runtime root mismatch; existing install and policy gates still apply.
3. Doctor and `session:start`: a direct check of the known path `<checkout>/node_modules/@deftai/directive-runtime`. Resolve its real path, cut it with `resolveLaunchingCheckoutRootFromPath` (pnpm normalisation included), and fail when the result is not the current checkout. Not a discovery walk.
4. Fixtures: junctioned runtime directory; junctioned whole `node_modules`; nested reverse link (`P` runtime linked to `P/.deft-scratch/worktrees/W/node_modules/@deftai/directive-runtime`) all give `foreign-runtime-link` and fail item 3; pnpm `.pnpm` link inside the checkout passes; a genuine mismatch keeps today's text. One fixture runs the real deposited launcher.
5. SEC-WT `rootsMatch` is unchanged.

issueCommentThread.body:
## Correction: the headline claim did not reproduce

I filed this from a code reading plus a worker's account, without reproducing it. Since then, one observation contradicts the headline:

- In a linked worktree on a branch cut from the delivery branch, with **two fencing active briefs** in `xbrief/active/` and **no `DEFT_ACTIVE_SCOPE` pin**, a worker made four Edit-tool writes to its own active brief. The hook allowed all four.
- So "refuses every Edit/Write as `multiple-eligible`" is not established. The `inspectActiveScope` → `partitionUnpinnedEligible` → `multiple-eligible` path exists in the code, but I have not shown when it fires in practice. Please treat that part as unconfirmed.

## What was observed

Same host session (Claude Code, Directive 0.129.6). The parent and two background workers each use their own linked worktree.

1. **One launch root per host session, rebound by any worker.** A worker ran `deft session:ready --project-root <its worktree> --session-id=<host id>`. After that, the parent's own Edit and Bash calls were refused, with its shell cwd in a different linked worktree:
   ```
   Directive hook refuse: payload project root does not match the launching checkout (payloadRoot=<other worktree> launchRoot=<worker's worktree>). Recovery: Prep the linked worktree (`deft swarm-worktrees prep --path <dest>`), then open that worktree as the host project root so launchRoot matches payloadRoot.
   ```
   Even `cd` back to the primary checkout was refused, so the parent's shell was locked until the root was rebound out of band. Workers in one host session share that launch root, so one worker's `session:ready` silently changes it for the parent and for every sibling.
2. **`git commit -F <file>` refused with no `-a` and no pathspec.** The worker staged a rename (`xbrief/active/<brief>` → `xbrief/completed/<brief>`), then ran `cd <worktree> && git commit -F <msg-file>`. It was refused three times with:
   ```
   Directive denied Bash: git commit -a/--all/-am/--include or pathspecs change the file set after the pre-tool index snapshot (#5656). Stage the intended paths first (git add …) then commit with -m/-F only — no -a/--all and no trailing pathspecs.
   ```
   Hypothesis, not verified: the pre-tool index snapshot is taken at the payload root (the host session's cwd or launch root), not at the worktree the command `cd`s into. The file set then appears to change.

## Retitled

I retitled this issue to the launch-root problem, which is the part that was observed. If the maintainers prefer, split the commit-snapshot refusal into its own issue.

## Still open as a question

Whether the write hook should bind a worktree's branch to its active story (`bindBranchToActiveStory`, #5855), as verify:ac and pre-push already do. That would matter if `multiple-eligible` does fire for writes. A reproduction would settle it.

## Follow-up: the commit refusal is about command shape, not the root

The hypothesis in my previous comment (point 2) was wrong. With the shell cwd already in the linked worktree, the same staged rename was refused when `git commit -F <file>` sat inside a compound command (`git commit -F <file> 2>&1 | tail -5; git log --oneline -2`), with the same #5656 message. The very next call, a standalone `git commit -F <file>`, from the same cwd and with the same index, committed normally.

The worker's earlier refusals all used `cd <worktree> && git commit -F <file>`. So the trigger looks like `git commit` inside a compound command. Under the #5656 index-snapshot check, the message then wrongly blames `-a`/`--all` or trailing pathspecs.

That makes it a separate, smaller problem from the shared launch root (point 1), which still stands. The misleading message is worth fixing either way: the refusal should say that a compound command was the reason. Agents whose shell cwd does not persist between calls (Claude Code subagents) have to `cd <worktree> && …`, so they cannot commit at all under this rule.

- Rewriting host hook deposits to the latest session:ready --project-root

Keeping a worker from displacing the parent’s launch root is a reasonable goal, but the draft does not yet identify the production mechanism that changes it. The pinned code derives launchRoot from executable location, while the proposal describes a session-id invariant. Keeping SEC-WT unchanged also means siblings rooted elsewhere remain denied; preserving the parent does not make those siblings usable. > **Correction (see the first comment):** the headline below, that two fencing active briefs make the write hook refuse every Edit, did not reproduce. A later observation shows Edits allowed in that state. The observed problem is the shared launch root, described in the comment.

## Summary

When two or more active briefs on the delivery branch each declare a `file_scope`, the PreToolUse write hook refuses every Edit/Write as `multiple-eligible`, in every worktree, whatever file is written. The hook can learn which story a write belongs to only from the `DEFT_ACTIVE_SCOPE` process environment or a spawn `boundPath`. It does not use the branch-to-story binding that the runtime already has (`bindBranchToActiveStory`, #5855).

Directive version: 0.129.6 (OVPR layout). Host: Claude Code, background `Agent` workers, one isolated worktree per worker.

## How it happens

1. A two-story swarm follows #4714: each selected brief is active on `origin/<deliveryBranch>` before launch. The two stories have different `file_scope`s.
2. Each worker runs in its own linked worktree, on a branch that names its issue (for example `feat/<N>-...` and `chore/<N>-complete`).
3. Any branch cut from the delivery branch now has both briefs in `xbrief/active/`.
4. Every Edit/Write in either worktree is denied with the `multiple-eligible` message, including edits to files that only one story's `file_scope` names, and edits to the worker's own brief during completion.

## Why the existing recovery does not work

- `DEFT_ACTIVE_SCOPE` is read from the host process environment. On Claude Code every background worker runs in the parent's process and shares one environment, so a worker cannot pin its own story, and a parent pin applies to every worker at once.
- Setting the pin needs a host restart, and with one shared pin the cohort becomes serial.
- `scope:stamp-evidence` writes only `test`/`review` evidence, so it cannot record the `deploy`/`observed_behavior` evidence a completion needs.
- The remaining path is a write through a shell form the hook does not classify (for example a short script that edits the JSON). That bypasses the gate. Workers reached for it twice in one cohort, once on a product source file and once on the brief, because no sanctioned path was left.

## Code pointers (vendor/directive-core/dist)

- `hooks/dispatcher.js`: direct writes call `inspectActiveScope(effectiveRoot, { env, boundPath? })`. `boundPath` is set only for spawn tools.
- `hooks/scope.js`, `inspectActiveScope`: with no pin, `partitionUnpinnedEligible` leaves every fencing brief in contention, so more than one fencing brief gives `denyKind: "multiple-eligible"`.
- `hooks/scope.js`, `bindBranchToActiveStory` (#5855): binds a branch to one active brief by `plan.id` segment, then by a single repo-scoped issue token. It is used by `resolveSoftMissingAcTargets` (verify:ac) and by the pre-push path (`preflight-gh/pre-push.js`), but not by the write hook.

## Prior art

#4880 (closed) fixed the multiple-active recovery text, stopped spawn from suggesting promote-then-activate, and partitioned out briefs with no `file_scope`. It did not give the write path a way to bind a worktree to its story, so this case remains.

## Proposed fix

Before falling back to `multiple-eligible`, let the write hook bind the worktree's current branch to its active story with `bindBranchToActiveStory`, as verify:ac and pre-push already do. Keep fail-closed when the binding refuses (no token, several tokens, several owners). Optionally also accept a per-worktree pin file, so hosts whose workers share one process environment can pin per worker.

## Acceptance

- Two fencing active briefs for issues A and B are on the delivery branch. In a worktree on a branch that names A, an Edit to a path in A's `file_scope` is allowed, and an Edit to a path only in B's `file_scope` is denied by the fence.
- A branch that names no issue, or several, still gets `multiple-eligible` (fail closed).
- The worker can edit its own active brief during completion without a process-wide pin.
